subject: Archaeology
title: The Copper Age: Metal Begins
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Copper Age: Metal Begins usable.

hook.text: Before bronze, before iron, people figured out that green rocks could be melted into copper — and shaped into tools.

buildup.text: The oldest smelted copper comes from Serbia, dating to about 5000 BCE. It was soft, but it could be resharpened.

discovery.text: Copper axes and ornaments spread through Europe and the Middle East. Metalworking became a specialized craft.

twist.text: Ötzi the Iceman carried a copper axe in 3300 BCE. Chemical analysis traced its copper to Tuscany — 300 miles away.

climax.text: Copper was too soft for heavy work but proved that metals could be extracted from rock. Bronze and iron followed.

punchline.text: Someone melted a green rock and got a knife.

quiz.question: What did Ötzi the Iceman's copper axe reveal?
options: Copper tools were only used by elite warriors
Chemical analysis traced its copper 300 miles to Tuscany, showing long-distance trade
Copper was more durable than bronze for cutting tools

details.summary: The Chalcolithic or Copper Age marks humanity's first use of metal, beginning around 5500 BCE. Early copper was hammered cold from native nuggets before smelting was discovered. Copper tools were softer than stone but easier to reshape, launching the age of metallurgy.
details.whyItMatters: Copper marked the transition from stone to metal technology. Though copper tools were often inferior to stone ones, the discovery of smelting was the crucial first step toward bronze, iron, and all subsequent metal technologies.
takeaways: The Copper Age began around 5500 BCE with native copper working
Smelting was discovered later, enabling copper extraction from ore
Copper launched the metallurgical tradition leading to bronze and iron

faq.question: Were copper tools better than stone tools?
faq.answer: Not always. Copper is softer than flint and dulls quickly. Copper's advantage was reshaping — a broken copper tool could be remelted and recast, while a broken stone tool was useless. Copper also had prestige value and was used for ornaments and status items.

faq.question: How was smelting discovered?
faq.answer: Probably accidentally in pottery kilns or campfires where copper-bearing rocks were present. When certain green minerals were heated to high temperatures, metallic copper pooled out. Recognizing and replicating this process launched deliberate metallurgy.
